title: Adaptive POP affinity using percentile-delta and network escrow for model-variant fallback
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent cross-POP p95 spikes caused by short-lived network degradation (packet loss, retransmits) that are not well-captured by raw p95 alone. Current routing uses static percentile thresholds which either overreact to short blips (causing churn) or underreact to sustained degradation (bad UX).

Proposal: Implement an adaptive POP affinity scorer that fuses p50/p95 percentile deltas with a lightweight 'network escrow' health signal (packet loss rate, connection resets, in-flight retry rate). The scorer will: 1) compute short (30s) and medium (5m) percentile windows for p50/p95 and derive a percentile-delta metric (p95_delta = p95_short - p95_medium); 2) compute a network escrow score that increases when packet loss or retransmit ratio exceeds safe thresholds, but decays over an escrow window to avoid overreaction to single-measurement spikes; 3) combine signals with heteroskedastic weighting (variance-aware) so POPs with high p95 variance get penalized proportionally more; 4) emit a ranked POP list and a confidence band that the router uses to steer traffic and to select a fallback model variant (e.g., quantized-lowmem or lower-context variant) when the top POP confidence is below threshold.

Why different: Instead of single-threshold gating, this approach uses percentile-delta (sudden changes relative to baseline), variance weighting (avoid punishing naturally noisy POPs), and a decaying escrow that provides short-term protection against flapping. It also ties routing confidence directly to model-variant selection to preserve availability with graceful quality tradeoffs.

Data sources: edge telemetry (p50/p95 histograms), infra metrics (packet loss, tcp_retransmits), request traces (latency + retries), KV cache hit rates to know locality effects.

Operational knobs: percentile window sizes, escrow decay half-life, variance-sensitivity alpha, fallback confidence threshold, canary ramp percentages for variant fallback, cooldown periods for POP moves.

Trade-offs and risks: More complexity in decisioning + more telemetry fusion increases operational surface. Incorrect weighting could bias traffic away from cheaper POPs and cost us. We must be careful with telemetry freshness and missing data: fall back to conservative routing if telemetry is stale.

Metrics to monitor post-rollout: p95 latency across global routes, cross-POP request churn rate, fallback-variant utilization, model quality deltas (via evals), and error rates in routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scorer computed per-POP once every 15s in prod with <100ms median compute latency.
- Demonstrated 5-10% reduction in p95 tail on synthetic packet-loss experiments in EU/US regions without increasing churn >2%.
- Fallback variant triggers only when top-POP confidence < 0.6 and fallback path success rate > 99% for 15m.
- No increase in 5xx error rate attributable to routing decisions after 72h canary.
- Unit and integration tests for percentile-delta, escrow decay, and variance weighting present in repo and passing CI.
- Ops runbook updated with thresholds, rollback steps, and dashboard links.
implementation_notes:
Components:
- telemetry-aggregator: new job to maintain short/medium percentile windows (30s/5m) per POP and emit p50/p95 deltas.
- escrow-service: stream processor that computes network escrow (packet_loss, retransmit_ratio) with an exponential decay buffer and outputs normalized escrow_score [0,1].
- scorer-service: stateless API that fuses percentile-delta, escrow_score, and p95 variance into a final pop_score and confidence. Exposed over internal gRPC for router.
- router-adaptor: small change to router to accept ranked list + confidence and apply steer/fallback policy.
- fallback-controller: maps confidence -> model-variant decision (quantized-lite, lower-context) and handles canary/rollout.

Key algorithms: percentile_delta = clamp(p95_short - p95_medium, -inf, inf); variance_penalty = sigmoid(variance * alpha); final_score = base_rank - w1 * percentile_delta - w2 * escrow_score - variance_penalty. We will tune w1/w2/alpha in staging via grid search.

Testing plan: unit tests for decay semantics, integration tests with synthetic telemetry, A/B canary (10% traffic) in one POP then expand. Benchmarks: measure scorer CPU, median latency, and memory.

Operational considerations: ensure scorer falls back to static affinity if telemetry stale >60s. Add alerting for escrow_score > 0.7 sustained > 2m.

Repo: infra/telemetry, runtime/scorer, router/adapter. Follow runtime-1.20 release branch for rollout.
